query_text: Can planets orbit twin star systems?

messages.content: Can planets orbit twin star systems?

message.content:
Yes. **Planets can orbit twin star systems**, and astronomers call these **circumbinary planets** when the planet orbits both stars together.[4][7]

There are also planets in **binary systems** that orbit just one of the two stars; these are called **S-type** or **circumstellar** orbits.[1][2] In addition, a planet can orbit both stars at a larger distance in a stable **P-type** orbit, and NASA notes that binary systems can host planets with “two stars in their skies.”[2][7]

These orbits are not just theoretical: confirmed circumbinary planets have been found, and one source notes that astronomers have discovered around 50 confirmed exoplanets on S-type orbits as well.[1][4] Stability depends on the stars’ masses and separation, so not every twin-star system can keep a planet for long periods.[1][2]
